title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(T>0\) and \(0<\beta<1/8\), and set
	\(m_0:=\mu_0(\overline D)\).
	We write \(\operatorname{E}_{x,\pi}\) for joint expectation over the reflected
	Brownian motion started from \(x\) and the environment started from its
	stationary distribution \(\pi\).
	
	Under the common-reference coupling used in
	Section~\ref{sec:homogenization}, in which the switching and homogenized
	models are built from the same reflected Brownian motion, put
	\[
	R_\varepsilon(t)
	:=
	\left|
	W^+_{\gamma_\varepsilon(t)}
	-
	W^+_{\gamma_0(t)}
	\right|
	+
	\left|
	K_\varepsilon(t)-K_0(t)
	\right|.
	\]
	The uniform spatial estimate
	\eqref{eq:uniform-process-rate}, with \(p=1\), and the maximal
	killing estimate obtained in the proof of
	Theorem~\ref{thm:SE_homogenization_1} give
	\begin{equation}
		\label{eq:forward-proof-coupling-bound}
		\sup_{x\in\overline D}
		\operatorname{E}_{x,\pi}
		\left[
		\sup_{0\le t\le T}R_\varepsilon(t)
		\right]
		\le C\varepsilon^\beta.
	\end{equation}
	The constant is uniform in \(x\): the averaging estimates follow from
	Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-averaging} and
	Lemma~\ref{lem:short-time-growth-local-time}, uniformly in the starting
	point, while Proposition~\ref{prop:Holder} provides the required uniform
	H\"older-moment bounds. Thus the spatial and killing estimates used in
	\eqref{eq:forward-proof-coupling-bound} have constants depending only on
	\(D,T,Q,\rho,\kappa,\beta\), and not on \(x,\varepsilon\), or \(\mu_0\).
	
	For a bounded Lipschitz function \(f\), the duality definitions
	\eqref{eq:forward-epsilon-duality} and
	\eqref{eq:forward-zero-duality} give
	\[
	\int_{\overline D}
	f\,d\bigl(\mu_t^{\varepsilon,\alpha}-\mu_t^0\bigr)
	=
	\int_{\overline D}
	\bigl(
	u_\alpha^\varepsilon(t,x;f)-u^0(t,x;f)
	\bigr)\,\mu_0(dx).
	\]
	If \(\|f\|_{\mathrm{BL}}\le1\), then
	\(\|f\|_\infty\le1\) and \(\operatorname{Lip}(f)\le1\).
	Consequently, \eqref{eq:Y-difference-bound} implies, for every fixed
	environment,
	\[
	\left|
	u_\alpha^\varepsilon(t,x;f)-u^0(t,x;f)
	\right|
	\le
	\operatorname{E}_x^W\!\left[R_\varepsilon(t)\right].
	\]
	Since \(\mu_0\) is nonnegative, it follows that
	\[
	\left|
	\int_{\overline D}
	f\,d\bigl(\mu_t^{\varepsilon,\alpha}-\mu_t^0\bigr)
	\right|
	\le
	\int_{\overline D}
	\operatorname{E}_x^W\!\left[R_\varepsilon(t)\right]\,\mu_0(dx).
	\]
	The right-hand side does not depend on \(f\). Taking the supremum over
	\(\|f\|_{\mathrm{BL}}\le1\) therefore yields
	\begin{equation}
		\label{eq:forward-proof-BL-bound}
		d_{\mathrm{BL}}
		\bigl(\mu_t^{\varepsilon,\alpha},\mu_t^0\bigr)
		\le
		\int_{\overline D}
		\operatorname{E}_x^W\!\left[R_\varepsilon(t)\right]\,\mu_0(dx).
	\end{equation}
	
The suprema used here are measurable. Indeed, the bounded-Lipschitz unit
ball is uniformly bounded and equicontinuous. By the Arzel\`a--Ascoli
theorem, its closure in \(C(\overline D)\) is compact; see
\cite[Theorem~4.43]{folland1999real}. Moreover, the unit ball is closed in
the uniform norm. Indeed, if \(f_n\to f\) uniformly and
\(\|f_n\|_{\mathrm{BL}}\le1\), then
\[
\|f\|_\infty=\lim_{n\to\infty}\|f_n\|_\infty
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{Lip}(f)
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{Lip}(f_n).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\|f\|_{\mathrm{BL}}
=
\|f\|_\infty+\operatorname{Lip}(f)
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\bigl(
\|f_n\|_\infty+\operatorname{Lip}(f_n)
\bigr)
\le1.
\]
Thus the bounded-Lipschitz unit ball is compact, hence separable, in the
uniform norm, and therefore admits a countable dense subset.

Moreover, for every \(f\in C(\overline D)\), the map
\[
t\longmapsto
\int_{\overline D} f\,d\mu_t^{\varepsilon,\alpha}
\]
is continuous, and similarly for \(\mu_t^0\). Hence the suprema over test
functions and over time may be taken over countable dense subsets.
	
	Taking the supremum in time in
	\eqref{eq:forward-proof-BL-bound}, then averaging over the environment
	and applying Tonelli's theorem, gives
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		&\operatorname{E}^\alpha
		\left[
		\sup_{0\le t\le T}
		d_{\mathrm{BL}}
		\bigl(\mu_t^{\varepsilon,\alpha},\mu_t^0\bigr)
		\right]
		\\
		&\qquad\le
		\int_{\overline D}
		\operatorname{E}^\alpha\operatorname{E}_x^W
		\left[
		\sup_{0\le t\le T}R_\varepsilon(t)
		\right]\,\mu_0(dx)
		\\
		&\qquad=
		\int_{\overline D}
		\operatorname{E}_{x,\pi}
		\left[
		\sup_{0\le t\le T}R_\varepsilon(t)
		\right]\,\mu_0(dx)
		\\
		&\qquad\le
		C m_0\varepsilon^\beta,
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	where the last inequality follows from
	\eqref{eq:forward-proof-coupling-bound}.
	This proves \eqref{eq:forward-BL-uniform}.
	The fixed-time estimate \eqref{eq:forward-BL-fixed} follows from
	\[
	\sup_{0\le t\le T}
	\operatorname{E}^\alpha
	d_{\mathrm{BL}}
	\bigl(\mu_t^{\varepsilon,\alpha},\mu_t^0\bigr)
	\le
	\operatorname{E}^\alpha
	\left[
	\sup_{0\le t\le T}
	d_{\mathrm{BL}}
	\bigl(\mu_t^{\varepsilon,\alpha},\mu_t^0\bigr)
	\right].
	\]
	
	Finally, for every \(\eta>0\), Markov's inequality gives
	\[
	\operatorname{P}^\alpha
	\left(
	\sup_{0\le t\le T}
	d_{\mathrm{BL}}
	\bigl(\mu_t^{\varepsilon,\alpha},\mu_t^0\bigr)
	>\eta
	\right)
	\le
	\frac{C m_0}{\eta}\varepsilon^\beta
	\longrightarrow0.
	\]
	Both forward measures have mass at most \(m_0\).
	Since \(\overline D\) is compact, the bounded-Lipschitz distance
	metrizes narrow convergence on this set of measures.
	This proves the asserted uniform-in-time convergence in probability.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(T>0\), and set
	\[
	a_f
	:=
	\left\|cf+\frac12\Delta f\right\|_\infty.
	\]
	As in the proof of
	Theorem~\ref{thm:improved-smooth-observable}, the proportionality condition
	\(\kappa_i=c\rho_i\) yields
	\[
	K_\varepsilon(t)=c\bigl(t-\gamma_\varepsilon(t)\bigr),
	\qquad
	K_0(t)=c\bigl(t-\gamma_0(t)\bigr).
	\]
	For a fixed environment, apply It\^o's formula to
	\(F(s,x)=e^{cs}f(x)\) at the bounded stopping times
	\(\gamma_\varepsilon(t)\) and \(\gamma_0(t)\).
	The Neumann condition removes the boundary local-time term.
	Taking expectations and subtracting the two identities yields
	\[
	u_\alpha^\varepsilon(t,x;f)-u^0(t,x;f)
	=
	\operatorname{E}_x^W
	\left[
	\int_{\gamma_0(t)}^{\gamma_\varepsilon(t)}
	e^{-c(t-s)}
	\left(cf+\frac12\Delta f\right)(W_s^+)\,ds
	\right],
	\]
	where the integral is understood in the oriented sense.
	
	Both inverse clocks are at most \(t\), and \(c\ge0\).
	Thus \(e^{-c(t-s)}\le1\) on the interval between them, and
	\begin{equation}
		\label{eq:forward-proof-smooth-clock-bound}
		\left|
		u_\alpha^\varepsilon(t,x;f)-u^0(t,x;f)
		\right|
		\le
		a_f\operatorname{E}_x^W
		\left|
		\gamma_\varepsilon(t)-\gamma_0(t)
		\right|.
	\end{equation}
	Using duality and the nonnegativity of \(\mu_0\), we obtain
	\begin{equation}
		\label{eq:forward-proof-smooth-duality-bound}
		\left|
		\int_{\overline D}
		f\,d\bigl(\mu_t^{\varepsilon,\alpha}-\mu_t^0\bigr)
		\right|
		\le
		a_f\int_{\overline D}
		\operatorname{E}_x^W
		\left|
		\gamma_\varepsilon(t)-\gamma_0(t)
		\right|\,\mu_0(dx).
	\end{equation}
	
	The fixed-time clock estimate
	\eqref{eq:fixed-time-gamma-L2-rate} holds uniformly in the starting
	point, by
	Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-averaging} and
	Lemma~\ref{lem:short-time-growth-local-time}.
	Consequently, Tonelli's theorem and Lyapunov's inequality give
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		&\sup_{0\le t\le T}
		\operatorname{E}^\alpha
		\left|
		\int_{\overline D}
		f\,d\bigl(\mu_t^{\varepsilon,\alpha}-\mu_t^0\bigr)
		\right|
		\\
		&\qquad\le
		a_f\int_{\overline D}
		\sup_{0\le t\le T}
		\operatorname{E}_{x,\pi}
		\left|
		\gamma_\varepsilon(t)-\gamma_0(t)
		\right|\,\mu_0(dx)
		\\
		&\qquad\le
		a_f\int_{\overline D}
		\sup_{0\le t\le T}
		\left(
		\operatorname{E}_{x,\pi}
		\left|
		\gamma_\varepsilon(t)-\gamma_0(t)
		\right|^2
		\right)^{1/2}\,\mu_0(dx)
		\\
		&\qquad\le
		C a_f\,\mu_0(\overline D)\,\varepsilon^{1/4}.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	This proves \eqref{eq:forward-improved-fixed}.
	
	For the uniform estimate, the inverse-clock comparison
	\eqref{eq:fixed-time-inverse-bound} gives
	\[
	\sup_{0\le t\le T}
	\left|
	\gamma_\varepsilon(t)-\gamma_0(t)
	\right|
	\le
	\sup_{0\le r\le T}
	\left|
	\int_0^r
	\bigl(\rho(\alpha_{s/\varepsilon})-\overline\rho\bigr)\,dL_s
	\right|.
	\]
	Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-averaging} with
	\(A=L\), \(h=\rho-\overline\rho\), and \(\vartheta=1/2\), we obtain
	\[
	\sup_{x\in\overline D}
	\operatorname{E}_{x,\pi}
	\left[
	\sup_{0\le t\le T}
	\left|
	\gamma_\varepsilon(t)-\gamma_0(t)
	\right|^2
	\right]
	\le
	C\varepsilon^{1/2}
	\bigl(1+|\log\varepsilon|\bigr)^2.
	\]
	Taking the supremum in time in
	\eqref{eq:forward-proof-smooth-duality-bound}, then using again Tonelli's
	theorem and Lyapunov's inequality, gives
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		&\operatorname{E}^\alpha
		\left[
		\sup_{0\le t\le T}
		\left|
		\int_{\overline D}
		f\,d\bigl(\mu_t^{\varepsilon,\alpha}-\mu_t^0\bigr)
		\right|
		\right]
		\\
		&\qquad\le
		a_f\int_{\overline D}
		\operatorname{E}_{x,\pi}
		\left[
		\sup_{0\le t\le T}
		\left|
		\gamma_\varepsilon(t)-\gamma_0(t)
		\right|
		\right]\,\mu_0(dx)
		\\
		&\qquad\le
		a_f\int_{\overline D}
		\left(
		\operatorname{E}_{x,\pi}
		\left[
		\sup_{0\le t\le T}
		\left|
		\gamma_\varepsilon(t)-\gamma_0(t)
		\right|^2
		\right]
		\right)^{1/2}\,\mu_0(dx)
		\\
		&\qquad\le
		C a_f\,\mu_0(\overline D)\,
		\varepsilon^{1/4}\bigl(1+|\log\varepsilon|\bigr).
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	Absorbing \(a_f\) into the constant \(C_f\) proves
	\eqref{eq:forward-improved-uniform}.
	Taking \(f\equiv1\) gives the stated bounds for the total surviving mass.
